question: How do Helium, Mimi, and Moshi's token streams work together to support full-duplex dialogue?
answer: Moshi employs Helium as its 7B parameter text language model backbone to drive the system's reasoning and dialogue generation [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 6] [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 41, §7 Conclusion]. Mimi functions as a semantic-acoustic neural audio codec that encodes audio into discrete units with low frame rates, ensuring compatibility with real-time generation [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 41, §7 Conclusion]. To support full-duplex dialogue, Moshi utilizes a hierarchical multi-stream architecture that models both the user’s and the system’s speech as separate, parallel streams of semantic and acoustic tokens [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 6] [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 1, §Abstract]. This parallel streaming approach eliminates the need for explicit speaker turns, enabling the system to handle overlapping speech, interruptions, and interjections inherent in real-time conversations [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 1, §Abstract].
